items.title: Jon Hendricks interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I learned from Art Tatum to hear every note in the chord. Because he would make me sing... Art had me come by his house after junior high school every day... he would play these phrases for me to sing.

ctx.x: You took a few years off in your early life, okay. We can understand that.

But Art and I played all the amateur shows around Toledo. He started out on the violin, you know. His ambition was to be another Jascha Heifetz. And his mother thought to help him with his violin she’d get him a piano. And he set down to that piano and boy —

items.title: Jon Hendricks interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: And they had this place called the Chateau La France which was a night club that featured a floor show with Art Tatum and me, and I was 11.

ctx.x: What kind of work were you able to do or allowed to do in the clubs?

Well I worked for the local gangsters, the Licavolian mob ran Ohio and part of Illinois. And the Purple Gang ran southern Michigan and the Detroit area. So Michigan was wet and Ohio was dry. So the Licavolis would run liquor down from Michigan into Ohio, into Toledo. And they had this place called the Chateau La France which was a night club that featured a floor show with Art Tatum and me, and I was 11. items.title: Jon Hendricks — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: We did two shows a night for two years I sang with him.

ctx.x: Yeah. It was not that I had some aptitude. I really had a true bent towards music. It was always – I was working practically from birth. As I told you, I never had a childhood. While other kids went to play baseball, basketball – went junking, we called it: gathering up old pieces of wire and metals and taking them and selling them for enough money to go to the movies, I would very seldom have a chance to do things like that, because I had to go to Art Tatum’s house when I was in junior high school.
